question: Ashoka mentions in his inscription that he conquered Kalinga _________ after becoming the king.
solution:
The correct answer is __**eight years.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Mauryan Empire**:

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya **was the **founder **of the Mauryan Empire.
 
• He is referred to in Greek sources as **Sandrokottos.**
 
• In 321 BC, he **defeated Dhana Nanda **and took the throne with the aid of a politically astute and clever Brahmin named **Kautilya**.
 
• **Megasthenes **served as the Greek representative in the court of Chandragupta.
 
• He led an expansionist policy that subjugated nearly all of modern-day India, **except **a few isolated areas in the far south and **Kalinga.**
 
• **Bindusara **is the second Mauryan Empire ruler.
 
• 297–273 BC was his rule period.
 
• He was also called **Amitraghata** (Slayer of foes).
 
• **Ashoka mentions in his inscription **that he **conquered Kalinga after becoming the king for eight years.**
 
• **Kalinga **was a region located in **present-day Odisha **and parts of **Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• Ashoka established **Ujjain and Takshashila **(later Taxila) as the **regional capitals **of his kingdom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Ashoka Maurya:**

 
• He was one of the **most powerful emperors of the Maurya dynasty **in ancient India, **ruling from 268 to 232 BCE**.
 
• The **conquest of Kalinga **was a major event in Ashoka's reign as it **resulted in the loss of over 100,000 lives **and left many more injured and displaced.
 
• He became deeply remorseful and **turned to Buddhism a****fter the war**, adopting a policy of non-violence and compassion towards all living beings.
 
• His **rock edicts and inscriptions**, which were written in various languages including Prakrit and Greek, **provide valuable insights into his life and teachings.******
 
• He designated representatives, referred to as the **dhamma mahamatta**, to spread the word and instruct people in dhamma.
 
• He also sent his children to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism.
